findings.finding: The 110/240 isolated DC maxima and complex dry gains are authored ideal binary64 calculations. Source uses Rust f32 and has downstream reverb/nonlinear output. Neither a full-bank/global measured peak nor physical bridge calibration, retuning or realism improvement follows.

Analytically empty bins retain an undefined transfer ratio despite floating residues. Weak excitation and cropped finite convolution invalidate naive identification under the displayed conditions; no universal cutoff or arbitrary transient-STFT ratio is established.

Unequal reversed two taps share all-frequency magnitudes and fail all eight integer circular-shift comparisons. This is not a universal phase-retrieval impossibility theorem. Centroid difference supplies no pure-delay, group-delay, audibility or preference result.

SetClass transforms a canonical spectral prime-form vector; keeping its phase cannot restore removed original transposition. The separate actual-chroma alignment path and audio time-domain transforms have distinct inputs and invariances.
Production plan explicitly records that it followed initial source reading, calculations and English drafting. It is not an advance preregistration.

exercise_answer_checks.checked_conclusion: Additive feedback gives recurrence a2=-0.9025 but denominator coefficient +0.9025 for the 110 Hz section. Numerator g=0.08 is not a frequency-independent gain; the five listed radii below one establish only ideal isolated linear stability.

The peak cosine cos(omega0)*(1+r^2)/(2*r) exceeds one for the 110 and 240 Hz parameters at Fs44100, so the constrained isolated maximum is DC. For 110, gains are about29.268259 at DC and27.306424 at110. Pole angle, isolated maximum, bank response and full nonlinear engine are distinct; binary64 arithmetic does not reproduce Rust f32.

Take the magnitude of0.55+0.45*sum(Hi), retaining complex responses. At110Hz the result34.953699 is below the magnitude-only upper bound35.364828. Triangle equality requires aligned contributing phases, including the positive direct path.

An ideal steady LTI input containing only82.4069 and164.8138Hz retains those frequencies with complex gains. A110Hz pole parameter supplies no additional sustained input-driven line; a decaying startup natural response and downstream nonlinear behavior are separate questions.

Analytically zero input/output at bin1 gives an undefined, unmeasured ratio rather than rejection gain0. Tiny floating residues do not identify it. Adding output coefficient0.01 to input1e-6 yields10000.75-0.25i; acquisition needs adequate excitation and a declared noise/conditioning policy, not a universal cutoff.

Reversed unequal taps A[0.75,0.25] and B[0.25,0.75], padded to8, share magnitude squared5/8+(3/8)cos(omega) at every real frequency. Their samples differ, and none of eight integer circular shifts matches them; the minimum maximum sample mismatch is0.25. Other invariances are not excluded.

At k2 A=0.75-0.25i and B=0.25-0.75i have equal magnitude0.790569415 but phases about-0.321750554/-1.249045772. DC is+1 for both; Nyquist is+0.5/-0.5. Complex phase distinguishes this pair; decibels cannot restore it. Zero-magnitude phase needs a separate undefined policy.

The positive-exponential1/N inverse reconstructs each full complex spectrum within numerical tolerance. Setting phases to zero before inversion invents a third choice. This finite full-transform counterexample is not a universal impossibility claim about constrained overlapping magnitude-STFT retrieval.

Both energies are5/8. Weighted squared-sample centroids are0.1 and0.9 sample, differing by0.8. This descriptor proves neither a pure delay/group-delay curve nor audibility, listener preference or guitar improvement.
